identity.name: Sucrose esters of fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Non-ionic sucrose fatty acid ester emulsifier mixture (mono-, di-, tri-esters)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic sucrose esters reduce oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize dispersed phases; depending on formulation they also modify texture and coating behavior.
common_food_categories: Dairy analogues and frozen dairy desserts
Coffee/tea beverages with added dairy ingredients
Protective coatings on selected fresh fruits

adi.basis: Group ADI for sucrose esters of fatty acids (E473) and sucroglycerides (E474), used in EFSA 2010/2012/2018/2023 assessments.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA follow-up in 2023 reported that updated exposure estimates can exceed the group ADI in many population groups, while also noting E473 was not reported as used in specific infant formula categories assessed.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-30 mg/kg bw/day for sucrose esters of fatty acids and sucroglycerides (1997 entry), with 2020 follow-up exposure commentary.

concerns.summary: Regulatory exposure assessments (EFSA and JECFA) repeatedly identified high-end intake scenarios in children/toddlers that exceed the group ADI, indicating a risk-management concern for heavy consumers.

Cell-model work indicates sucrose esters can alter epithelial permeability and membrane behavior at non-toxic concentrations; this is mechanistic evidence of biological activity but not direct proof of adverse clinical outcomes at food exposure levels.

no_concern_confirmed: A 2-year rat feeding study reported no treatment-related carcinogenicity or chronic toxicity up to 5% of diet.
No IARC Monographs classification entry was found for E473/sucrose esters of fatty acids in the current IARC list dataset.
Regulatory authorities continue to authorize E473 with exposure/specification controls rather than withdrawal.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA and JECFA reported that high-end modeled intakes can exceed ADI values; both sources also note conservative assumptions likely overestimate true exposure in some scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E473 remains approved in major frameworks, but repeated ADI exceedance signals in modeled high consumers (especially children) and continued exposure-refinement caveats argue for a moderate, not limited, risk tier.
key_factors: EFSA 2023 follow-up: exposure estimates exceed group ADI in many groups
EFSA 2018 refined assessment: exceedance especially in toddlers/children
JECFA 2020 comment: high estimate in children exceeded group ADI by about fourfold
No IARC listing identified for E473
